EXTRA CLASS · AGES 2–5 · 15 CARDS · 48 WORDS

Look & Learn.

Fifteen picture cards, four words each, and one tiny move on every picture — point at the moon, waddle like a duck, balance like a flamingo. This is the school’s lightest class: no sequence, no worksheets, just looking, saying and a little moving, for children from two to five.

Start with card 01 ↓Cover first, then cards 01–15 in order.
HOW LOOK & LEARN WORKS

Look at the picture, say the word, do the move.

Every card is a sheet of four mini-cards, and every mini-card does the same three things: shows one big clear picture, names it in one word, and hands you a move — the little action pill in the middle. Look & Point. Move & Count. Smell & Describe. You read the move, your child does it, and the word rides along on the action. Nothing here needs reading, printing or setting up; the whole method fits in the gap between lunch and shoes.

One card a sitting is plenty, and the order below is simply the order the cards were drawn. Each word on each card comes with what it names, where your child already meets it and one way to try it today — all on this page, so you land straight on the word your child just pointed at. Five of the forty-eight words (duck, banana, carrot, grapes and strawberry) already live on the library shelf in the school’s flashcards library, because a word should live in one home, not two.

WHERE THIS CLASS FITS

Three classes grow into these cards.

Look & Learn collects first words from three places on the Learning Path. The animal words (duck, bird, dog, cat, bee, owl) began in Animals and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds — Class 11. The fruit-and-vegetable words (banana, carrot, grapes, strawberry, pear, lemon, tomato, pumpkin) grew out of Fruits & Vegetables — Class 22. And the sky-and-season words (moon, star, cloud, raindrop, sun, leaf, acorn) belong beside Science, Nature & Discovery — Class 31. If your child is working through any of those classes, these cards are the pocket version — and if you are only here to look and say, that is the whole point.

Ages are a guide, not a test. Two-year-olds point and name; four-year-olds describe and count. Both are doing it right.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 01 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Moon Flashcard for Kids

The moon is the night light that was here first — children find it from windows, strollers and dark car rides, and it looks a little different every night. Card 01 shows it as a big round blue circle; card 09 brings it back as a yellow crescent, which is how it really looks half the month.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Point to the moon and say its name.”

The card’s own move: Look & Point.

Try it now

Tonight, step outside or find it from the window. When your child spots it, hold the moment — "There is the moon, can you say moon?" — then ask whether tonight’s moon is a circle or a banana curve.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 01 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Tree Flashcard for Kids

A tree is the tallest living thing on your street, and children watch it change all year — flowers, leaves, bare branches, back again. Card 01 asks your child to reach high like a tree; card 08 turns the same tree into one slow breath.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Reach high like a tree and count to five.”

Your move on this card: Move & Count.

Try it now

On the way to anywhere, pick one tree and be its shape: arms up for branches, wiggling fingers for leaves. Count to five while you reach — the card’s game, played against a real trunk.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 01 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Star Flashcard for Kids

A star is the smallest thing your child can point at in the whole sky — tiny, bright and gone by morning. Card 01 prints one plump yellow star among its four pictures; card 07 brings the same star back for a pointing game.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Find a star and name its colour.”

How the card says to play it: Find & Name.

Try it now

Cut a star from paper and hide it somewhere sneaky, then send your child hunting. Finding it is only half the job — naming its colour finishes the card’s game.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 01 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Flower Flashcard for Kids

A flower is the one plant a toddler is allowed to stop for — on the sidewalk, in the park, in the vase on the table. Card 01’s flower is pink with a yellow centre, drawn big enough to talk about petals.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Pretend to smell the flower and describe it.”

The move printed on the card: Smell & Describe.

Try it now

Pretend to smell the flower — a big sniff and a happy sigh — then pass it over for your child to smell too. Ask what it smells like; any answer, even "like pink", is a real description.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 02 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Ladybug Flashcard for Kids

A ladybug is the first insect children want to hold — red, dotted and harmless, landing on arms and book bags all summer. Card 02 counts its spots; card 09 asks for a closer look at the very same spots.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Look at the ladybug and count its spots.”

The card’s own move: Look & Count.

Try it now

Draw a ladybug together and take turns pressing one finger per spot while counting aloud. A real ladybug counts too — the answer changes every time, and that is the fun.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 02 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Turtle Flashcard for Kids

A turtle carries its house and never hurries — the perfect animal for a small child to copy. Card 02 turns your child into one: move slowly and say the name; card 15 brings the same green turtle back for another slow lap.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Move slowly like a turtle and say its name.”

Your move on this card: Move & Say.

Try it now

Crouch low, tuck your arms in and cross the room at turtle speed. Whoever says "turtle" on the way wins — and losing is just another lap.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 02 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Raindrop Flashcard for Kids

A raindrop is weather a child can hear — on the window, on the roof, tapping the umbrella. Card 02 draws one fat blue drop all by itself; card 15 looks at the same drop and asks how big it is.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Tap gently and listen for raindrops.”

The move printed on the card: Tap & Listen.

Try it now

Tap the window gently with one fingertip, then faster — light rain, heavy rain. Finish with one slow tap: "one raindrop." Your child will invent the sound effects; let them.

Kite Flashcard for Kids

A kite is the toy that turns wind into a game — dancing at the end of a string while your child runs underneath. Card 03’s kite is red with a ribbon tail; card 10’s is purple with little bows.

Say it together

“Move your hands like a kite flying.”

The card’s own move: Fly & Move.

Try it now

Arms up, fingers spread, and sail around the room like a kite in the wind — sway, dip, spin. A scarf held by one corner makes a fine kite whenever the real wind cooperates.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 03 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Whale Flashcard for Kids

A whale is the biggest animal your child will never meet at the park — enormous, gentle and famous for its songs. Card 03 draws one blue whale mid-spout, small enough to fit on a lap.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Pretend to swim like a whale.”

Your move on this card: Swim & Say.

Try it now

Lie on the floor, press your palms together and glide through the water. Come up for air with a big whoosh — that is the spout — then dive again.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 03 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Cactus Flashcard for Kids

A cactus is the plant that hugs back — prickly, patient and perfectly dressed for the desert. Card 03 draws a green one standing tall and asks your child to describe it, which is a thinking game dressed up as looking.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Look closely and describe the cactus.”

The move printed on the card: Look & Describe.

Try it now

Hands hovering near but never touching, pat the air around your child’s best cactus pose. Ask what would happen if you hugged it for real — the wince is the answer.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 04 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Cat Flashcard for Kids

A cat is the neighbour children meet before they can walk — asleep in windows, trotting along fences, entirely on its own schedule. Card 04’s orange cat is caught mid-stretch, and the stretch is the game.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Stretch like a cat and say its name.”

The card’s own move: Stretch & Say.

Try it now

Hands and knees on the floor, back up, bottom high: be a cat. Stretch long, yawn wide, purr loudly. Two stretches and the word is yours.

Butterfly Flashcard for Kids

A butterfly is the bug that starts as a caterpillar and turns into flight — magic your child can actually check in a picture book. Card 04’s butterfly is purple with wide wings; card 14’s is pink and asks for flapping hands.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Flap your hands and count to three.”

Your move on this card: Flap & Count.

Try it now

Fold your hands together, then open them for one wing-flap: one, two, three. Counting rides on the wings — three flaps, three claps, three butterflies.

Bear Flashcard for Kids

A bear is the biggest cuddle in the forest — brown, lumbering and asleep all winter. Card 14’s bear sits like a teddy and asks one question: how big?

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Look at the bear and describe its size.”

Try it now

Arms out: is the bear this big? Bigger! Stretch as wide as the room allows, then shrink down to cub size and hug yourself instead.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 14 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Balloon Flashcard for Kids

A balloon is a party on a string — weightless, bouncy and one squeeze away from a very loud goodbye. Card 14 holds one and breathes in; card 15 looks at the same purple balloon and names its colour.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Pretend to hold a balloon and breathe in.”

How the card says to play it: Hold & Breathe.

Try it now

Pat the balloon up, up, up — keep it off the floor and say the word on every pat. Then hold it still, breathe in slowly like the card says, and feel how calm looks.

LOOK & LEARN · CARD 15 OF 15 · AGES 2–5

Apple Flashcard for Kids

An apple is the first fruit most children name — in the lunchbox, on the teacher’s desk, red and round in every picture book. Card 15’s apple asks for its shape, which small fingers already know.

Teaching tips

Say it together

“Look at the apple and describe its shape.”

Try it now

Roll an apple slowly across the table: round and round it goes. Then trace its circle with one finger and say the word — snack and lesson in the same fruit.
